title: Spectral Battlefield Post-Processing Suite
description: A soldier patrols a haunted battlefield while a floating skull emanates ghostly energy. The user controls a multi-layered post-processing pipeline — toggling and tuning bloom, film grain, color grading, vignette, pixelation, and a custom ghost-pulse effect — to transform the scene from realistic combat footage into a supernatural horror aesthetic.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with EffectComposer post-processing. Load 'shared_assets/soldier.glb' positioned at origin playing its walk animation via AnimationMixer, and 'shared_assets/ScatteringSkull.glb' floating above and behind the soldier at (0, 3, -2), slowly orbiting the soldier in a 3-unit radius with a sinusoidal vertical bob. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 6) looking at the soldier. Add a dim ambient light (0x334455, 0.3) and a point light (0xff4400, 2) parented to the skull to cast eerie moving shadows. Enable renderer.shadowMap. Build an EffectComposer with RenderPass plus these passes the user controls via a dat.gui panel: (1) UnrealBloomPass — threshold (0-1, default 0.6), strength (0-3, default 1.5), radius (0-1, default 0.4); (2) ShaderPass with a custom Film Grain shader — intensity uniform (0-1, default 0.35); (3) ShaderPass for Color Grading — a tint uniform vec3 defaulting to greenish (0.6, 1.0, 0.7) and a contrast uniform (0.5-2.0, default 1.2); (4) ShaderPass for Vignette — darkness (0-2, default 1.5) and offset (0-2, default 0.9); (5) ShaderPass for Pixelation — pixelSize uniform (1-16, default 1 meaning off). Add a checkbox 'Ghost Pulse' that, when enabled, modulates bloom strength sinusoidally over time between 0.5 and 3.0 synced to the skull's orbit. The gui must have folders: 'Bloom', 'Film Grain', 'Color Grading', 'Vignette', 'Pixelation', 'Ghost Pulse'. Validate all parameters stay within specified ranges by clamping in the render loop. The scene background should be black. Ensure the animation loop updates AnimationMixer, skull orbit, ghost pulse logic, and EffectComposer rendering each frame. All shader uniforms must update from gui values every frame.
